gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham reads friendly and modern, with a big central band in each line and an s whose ends hang far from the spine. Woodgod is the one built to command attention; the body is built to be read.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Dependable and businesslike, Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, its curve endings keeping their distance. Woodgod does the shouting; this one does the steady talking.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height made for screens, and its curved letters keep wide, unclosed mouths. Woodgod brings vintage weight to the top, and the body text can be nudged up a size if it feels tight.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-sundanes: Crisp and compact, with e crossbars that open their mouths and almost no gap between x-height and capitals. Body text in Noto Sans Sundanese may want a size bump, since Woodgod already carries the heft.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Friendly at heart, Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in its curves, like the open bight of a rope. Woodgod commands the top with a wide channel into every bowl, while the body quietly handles the reading with its short ascender stems.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri reads crisp and tidy, with short ascenders and a tall x-height. Woodgod's wide-channeled bowls and near-capital lowercase give the heading a vintage swagger, while the body's open lower bowl on the a keeps the text line easy.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac has lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs. Woodgod is at its best as a vintage, commanding headline with wide channels into each bowl, while the body is best at its easy, wide-turning s shapes.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syriac-e: Woodgod's lowercase climbs so tall it nearly meets the capitals, with a wide channel into every bowl. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern follows with small caps under tall lowercase and curve endings far apart, so a long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-syriac-w: Vintage muscle meets modern polish here. Woodgod lets its tall lowercase loom over the page, while Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke and packs small letters thick with height like bundled cable.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Woodgod announces itself with a wide channel into every bowl and lowercase that nearly touches the capitals. Noto Sans Tagalog follows with a middle zone that dominates each line, and generous gaps in its curves.
